messages:
Soren: quick follow-up from the postmortem — we saw a recurring KV-cache growth pattern leading to OOMs. want to lock owners + short timeline for remediation (profiling, GC tweaks, limits, and a short-term guardrail).

Soren: current asks: 1) get heap+kv alloc traces from last 3 incidents; 2) try a reproducer in staging with longer retention; 3) evaluate slab vs fragmentation; 4) put per-shard soft limits and eviction policy; 5) add alert for sustained growth > 5%/min for 10m.

Lina: I can take #1 and #2. will start with pprof from the failing job and a full jemalloc dump. ETA tomorrow EOD.

Soren: thanks @Lina. please capture both allocation stack samples + object histograms. add link to traces in the ticket.

Lina: note: quick commands i'm running:

    gcore <pid> && jeprof --show_bytes /my/service /tmp/jeprof.heap > kv-alloc.html
    go tool pprof -svg /bin/service cpu.prof > cpu.svg

Soren: perfect. include a grep for heavy keys (large prefixes) — we've seen ~3 hot prefixes that bloat the cache.

Mike: i'll own #4 (per-shard soft limits + eviction policy). plan: implement a tunable soft_limit that transitions to LFU eviction before OOM. will open a draft PR with config knobs by Fri.

Katy: i'll do #5 (alerting) and a short-term cgroup memory cap for the most affected pool. rolling this as a canary to prod tomorrow morning.

Mike: question on evacuation semantics — should eviction be synchronous (on insert) or background async? synchronous likely spikes latency. leaning background. thoughts?

Soren: lean async with a fast-path sync eviction if free memory < 5%. keep latency SLOs. add safety: if eviction doesn't free >= 20% in 30s, fallback to model variant and circuit-break offending route.

Lina: for #3 (slab vs frag) initial signal: histogram shows many mid-sized objects ~1-4KB and a long tail. fragmentation likely contributing. i'll run fragmentation scan tomorrow and propose slab size changes.

Katy: ops-bot: scheduling note — i'll annotate the incident ticket with the planned canary time and rollback plan. ops-bot: any blocked changes?

ops-bot: deployment window reserved 03/12 08:00-09:00 UTC for canary. rollback hook created: deploy rollback tag kv-eviction-guard.

Soren: Risk/acceptance criteria: reduced incident recurrence (no OOMs for 14 days in same shard pattern) + CPU/latency regressions within 5% of baseline. if not met, escalate to deeper allocator changes.

Mike: opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-service/pull/412 — draft includes soft_limit, eviction queue, metrics (evicted_keys_total, eviction_latency_ms). feedback welcome.

Lina: uploading initial heap artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/trace/kv/199999-sh-1/heap-199999.tar.gz

Katy: alert rule:

    sum by(shard) (increase(kv_cache_bytes[10m])) / shard_size > 0.05

will fire when >5% growth over 10m. setting to notify #eng-runtime-page.

Soren: owner summary (putting owners inline):
- profiling + reproducer: Lina (ETA +1d)
- shard soft limits + eviction: Mike (PR by Fri)
- alerting + canary cap: Katy (canary tomorrow)
- final follow-up sync: Soren to run on Mon 03/15

Lina: one more ask — if anyone has a recent memprof that includes KV key sampling, pls drop here. helps map hot keys to code paths.

Mike: i'll add unit tests for eviction correctness and an e2e that simulates heavy prefix churn.

Katy: i'll post canary results in this thread after 2 hours of traffic. planning a quick rollback if eviction causes lat > 10% or fails to reduce mem by >=15% in canary.

Soren: great. last thing — let's add a quarterly check in on KV growth patterns (recurring incident pattern). i'll add a recurring calendar invite and a lightweight dashboard for top-10 prefixes by growth rate.

Katy: ack. created dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/kv/kv-growth (shared with eng-runtime).

ops-bot: reminder: incident ticket #INC-2387 updated with owners and links.

Soren: thanks all. short sync Monday with artifacts ready. :thumbsup:

Katy: :thumbsup: got it.

Mike: on it.

Lina: will post early findings tomorrow.
